items.statement: No baseline characteristics were statistically significant.
source: Full article, Abstract, Results

items.statement: The authors interpreted the results as showing modest improvement and maintenance of health status, with EQ‐5D‐5L data adding the patient perspective to primary-care program evaluation.
source: Full article, Discussion, paragraph 1

items.statement: The authors concluded that routine EQ‐5D‐5L implementation can inform decisions about program quality and service delivery and help primary-care programs respond to patient needs.
source: Full article, Conclusion

items.statement: Differential loss to follow-up could have occurred among patients who completed only the pre-program survey.
source: Full article, Strengths and Limitations, paragraph 1

items.statement: Missing data, the absence of a control arm, and the limited repeated-measure sample created methodological challenges.
source: Full article, Strengths and Limitations, paragraph 1

items.statement: The researchers could not link EQ‐5D‐5L data to other patient data, which limited the analysis.
source: Full article, Strengths and Limitations, paragraph 1

items.statement: The findings are not generalizable to other populations, although the authors considered them potentially transferable to similar primary-care programs.
